LESSON: REPORTING SKILLS

Grade: SNE  /  physical-impairment / PP2
Subject: General
Strand: Listening and Speaking
Topic 1.2: Reporting Skills
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 2

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Reporting Skills, part of Listening and Speaking in SNE  /  physical-impairment / PP2 General.

Key inquiry question: How is the weather today? 2. Which clothes do we wear on a rainy day?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

A. name different weather conditions,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Reporting Skills in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

B. report orally the weather conditions observed,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Reporting Skills in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

C. express appreciation of reporting incidences or happenings. • Name different weather conditions Learners with speech difficulties could use residual speech as they are lip read by the teacher or peers. ● Take a nature walk outside the classroom to observe the weather. Learners using mobility devices could be 1. How is the weather today? 2. Which clothes do we wear on a rainy day? 71 supported as they move during nature walks. ● Talk about the observed weather conditions in turns. ● Watch a video clip on the effect of different weather conditions. Light intensity could be adjusted for learners who are sensitive to light. ● Tell or use alternative mode of communication to express their view on the weather conditions observed, ● Learner talks about observed weather conditions from the clips or pictures. Learners with speech difficulties could use alternative modes of communication to express their views. ● Identify different activities done under different weather conditions, ● Identify negative effects of weather conditions, 72 ● Role-play a rainy day learner carrying umbrellas. Learners to be assigned roles according to their functional abilities ● Sing songs related to weather. Learners with speech difficulties could hum, mime or tap, clap or move with the rhythm of the song.

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

Follow your teacher’s guidance for group work, discussion, and practice on this topic.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Reporting Skills together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

Core competencies:

• Learning to learn: The learner takes a nature walk, observes the weather condition and persistently discovers more from

the environment about weather.

• Communication and collaboration: The learner role plays a rainy day carrying umbrellas while in communication with

others.

Values:

• Responsibility: The learner practices the importance of covering self with an umbrella when rainy during the role play.

• Unity: The learner learns to cooperate as they take turns to report observation findings after the nature walk.

Pertinent and Contemporary Issue(
s) :

Tolerance: The leaner acquires the life skill of patience as they walk around and observe the weather condition during nature

walk.

Link to other Activity Areas:

Reporting skills link to Environmental Activities where the learner observes weather during the nature walk and role plays use

of umbrella on a rainy day.
